findings.evidence: Rubric: keep bodies unexposed unless a consumer must unfold or compute, and ask for the missing lemma instead. `grep -rn 'theorem toFreeGroup_gen|toFreeGroup_mul|toFreeGroup_pow|theorem toWord_gen' TauCeti` → no matches; the file has no equation lemmas for either function.
findings.fix: Drop both `@[expose]`s and add public `@[simp]` equation lemmas in `Relator.lean`: `toWord_gen/inv/mul/pow/comm` and `toFreeGroup_gen/inv/mul/pow/comm`, each `:= (rfl)` so the statement is not left to defeq. `toFreeGroup_coxeterRelator` and `toWord_ofGenerators` then go through by `simp` without any body being public.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` on `toWord` (line 90) and `toFreeGroup` (line 104) exposes two recursive bodies to supply what equation lemmas should supply; no consumer in this PR unfolds or computes with them (the six `decide` examples are all about `yCoxeterMatrix`, and `toFreeGroup_coxeterRelator` is proved once inside `Relator`'s own... no, inside Coxeter.lean, where a simp set would do).

findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'YAdjacent_iff' TauCeti` → no match; `YAdjacent` at line 249 carries no `@[expose]` and the file is under `module`/`public section`, so the body is opaque outside this file (the PR's own description states bodies are not reducible outside their file without `@[expose]`).
findings.fix: Add `theorem YAdjacent_iff (p q i j : ℕ) : YAdjacent p q i j ↔ (i ≠ 0 ∧ yParent p q i = j) ∨ (j ≠ 0 ∧ yParent p q j = i) := Iff.rfl`, plus a `not_YAdjacent` criterion in terms of the arm arithmetic that downstream diagrams actually need.
findings.issue: `YAdjacent` is a `Prop`-valued `def` whose body is not exposed, and the file gives only introduction lemmas (`YAdjacent_one_zero`, `_secondArmHead_zero`, `_thirdArmHead_zero`, `YAdjacent_pred`) plus `.ne`. There is no elimination/iff form, so a consumer cannot prove `¬ YAdjacent p q i j` — the hypothesis of `yCoxeterMatrix_of_not_adjacent` (line 344), which covers the majority of matrix entries. The in-file `decide` examples work only because they are in the same module.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'coxeterRelators_eq\|y443Relators_eq\|ySpiderRelator_eq' TauCeti` → only `length_coxeterRelators_eq_div` and the `Y₄₄₃`-specific `y443SpiderRelator_eq`; in-file proofs use `rw [coxeterRelators]` / `rw [y443Relators]`, which downstream cannot do.
findings.fix: Add `ySpiderRelator_eq`, `y443Relators_eq`, and `coxeterRelators_eq` (each `:= (rfl)`), and mark `coxeterRelatorsOfList_cons` `@[simp]` so that it and the already-`@[simp]` `coxeterRelatorsOfList_nil` actually compute the list downstream.
findings.issue: Unexposed definitions without a `*_def` restatement, so consumers cannot unfold them: `ySpiderRelator` (line 356 — `y443SpiderRelator_eq` covers only the `Y₄₄₃` instance, leaving the roadmap's `Y₄₃₃` and Fischer spiders with no way to spell out their word), `y443Relators` (line 392 — cannot be decomposed, so `Relator.relatorSet_append` cannot be applied to it when the Monster row adds `Z = 1`), and `coxeterRelators` (line 156 — no lemma relating it to `coxeterRelatorsOfList`).

findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'toFreeGroup_ofGenerators' TauCeti` → no match; `relatorSet` at Relator.lean:113 is `{r | ∃ t ∈ l, t.toFreeGroup = r}`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem toFreeGroup_ofGenerators (x : α) (l : List α) : (ofGenerators x l).toFreeGroup = FreeGroup.of x * (l.map FreeGroup.of).prod` (or the fold form), by induction.
findings.issue: `Relator.ofGenerators` is characterized only by `toWord_ofGenerators`; there is no `toFreeGroup_ofGenerators`. Since `Relator.relatorSet` (line 113) is defined through `toFreeGroup`, the spider relator built from `ofGenerators` has no stated meaning as a free-group element, so no consumer can say what relation the spider imposes.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'GroupPresentation.mulEquivCoxeterGroup' TauCeti` → only the module docstring (line 49) and the definition (line 230); no `_apply`. `mathlib/Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Basic.lean:171` supplies `quotientMulEquivOfEq_mk`.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem GroupPresentation.mulEquivCoxeterGroup_apply (P) (M) (h) (i : Fin P.generatorCount) : P.mulEquivCoxeterGroup M h (PresentedGroup.of i) = M.simple i := QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq_mk _ _`.
findings.issue: `GroupPresentation.mulEquivCoxeterGroup` has no `_apply` lemma, unlike `mulEquivCoxeterGroup` which gets `mulEquivCoxeterGroup_apply` (line 222). Its body is a `QuotientGroup.quotientMulEquivOfEq` behind an unexposed `def`, so a consumer cannot track a generator through the equivalence — exactly what the pending Monster row needs in order to name the central involution `Z`.

findings.evidence: Lines 404-413: the two sibling lemmas use two different statement shapes for the same kind of fact.
findings.fix: State `(coxeterRelators (yCoxeterMatrix 4 4 4)).length = 91` and leave the `+ 1` to the docstring or to a `y444Relators` list, as `length_y443Relators` does.
findings.issue: `length_coxeterRelators_y444` is named as a length lemma but states `(coxeterRelators (yCoxeterMatrix 4 4 4)).length + 1 = 92`, baking the spider relator into an arithmetic identity. It does not give a consumer the count `91`, and breaks the parallel with `length_coxeterRelators_y433` (line 410), which states `= 66`.

findings.evidence: GroupPresentation.lean:92-109 vs Relator.lean:113-119: `{r | r ∈ P.relators.map FreeGroup.mk}` and `{r | ∃ t ∈ l, t.toFreeGroup = r}` are proved equal by `ext r; simp`.
findings.fix: Define `GroupPresentation.relatorSet (P) : Set _ := Relator.relatorSet P.transcribed`; `mem_relatorSet_iff` then becomes `Relator.mem_relatorSet` and `relatorSet_eq_relatorSet` disappears. Also drop `TauCeti.Relator.relatorSet` from Coxeter.lean's `## Main definitions` (line 36) — it is defined in `Relator.lean` and already listed there (Relator.lean:33).
findings.issue: `Relator.relatorSet` duplicates `GroupPresentation.relatorSet`: both denote the same set and their membership lemmas (`Relator.mem_relatorSet`, `GroupPresentation.mem_relatorSet_iff`) have identical right-hand sides, bridged by the new `relatorSet_eq_relatorSet`. Two same-named notions on the public surface with a bridge lemma between them invites divergence.

summary: The Coxeter relator list and Y-diagram data are the right surface, but several definitions ship with unexposed bodies and no characteristic lemma, so downstream consumers cannot use them: `YAdjacent` has no elimination form (making `yCoxeterMatrix_of_not_adjacent` unusable), `ySpiderRelator`/`y443Relators`/`coxeterRelators` have no `*_def`, `ofGenerators` has no `toFreeGroup` lemma, and the presentation-record equivalence has no `_apply`. `@[expose]` on `Relator.toWord`/`toFreeGroup` is used in place of the missing equation lemmas.
